title: Evaluating the glycolytic potential of mouse costimulated effector CD8+ T cells ex vivo
protocol: Euthanize OT-I mice according to your approved animal protocol.
Place mice on a clean dissection board.
Spray mice with 75% ethanol.
Make a sub-cutaneous incision using sterile scissors.
Remove the spleen from the abdomen, excising any excess of fat.
Place the spleen in a 12 well-plate filled with 2 mL of ice-cold BSS.
Crush the spleen using a syringe plunger over a 100 μm strainer placed on a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the strainer with ice-cold BSS and fill the 50 mL tube with the rinse.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 5 mL of NH4Cl for RBC lysis.
Incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Fill the 50 mL tube with BSS and gently mix.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend pellet in 200–500 μL of BSS if necessary.
Count splenocytes using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Transfer a small aliquot (at least 10^4 cells/well) to a flat-bottom 96 well plate.
Spin the plate at 400 g × 3 min at 4°C, then flick buffer off while the cell pellet remains.
Wash by adding 200 μL of FACS buffer, spin, and flick.
Add 10 μL of Fc block (42 μg/mL) and incubate for 1 min at 21°C–25°C.
Add 50 μL of the surface staining mix and incubate 30 min at 4°C.
Wash twice by adding approximately 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Resuspend in 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Acquire cells on a Flow Cytometer (e.g., an LSR II, BD).
Analyze using FlowJo.
Ensure that all CD8+ T cells are CD45.1+.
Verify that the CD8+ T cells express the transgenic TCR Vα2+ and Vβ5+.
Confirm that the recipient mice cells are CD45.2 to distinguish them from the donor cells.
Conduct quality control analysis to ensure less than 5% of CD4+ cells are present.
Ensure undetectable levels of B cells (B220/CD45R+).
Verify that cell activation as indicated by CD44+ is below 10%.
Confirm less than 20%-25% of the cells have undergone death.
Calculate the number of single live CD8+ OT-I cells using the specified formula.
Immediately after flow cytometry analysis, prepare splenocyte suspension from CD45.1+ Rag−/− OT-I mice such that each recipient mouse receives 0.5 × 10^6 CD8+ OT-I cells in 50–100 μL.
Inject the prepared splenocyte suspension into CD45.2+ C57BL/6J recipient mice using a 1 mL syringe with a 27 G x 1/2″ needle.
One day after adoptive transfer, inject ovalbumin (OVA) peptide specific for transgenic CD8+ T cells intraperitoneally (i.p.).
Simultaneously, inject costimulatory agonists α-CD134 (OX-40)/CD137 (4-1BB) mAbs to induce antigen-specific CD8+ T cell effector differentiation and survival.
Anesthetize C57BL/6J mice using isoflurane or other appropriate anesthetic.
Draw back the skin above the eye to allow the eye to protrude.
Insert the needle (bevel up) at an angle of about 45ᵒ to the conjunctival membrane.
Inject about 50 μL of the splenocyte suspension i.v. by retro-orbital injection into the retro-bulbar sinus.
Pause a second or so to avoid back pressure reflux.
Gently remove the needle to prevent bleeding or any eye injury.
Wait for the mice to recover from anesthesia.
Immunize the recipient mice with SIINFEKL and costimulatory antibodies (α-CD134/CD137) after 18–20 h.
Prepare the injection solution in sterile PBS containing 50 μg of SIINFEKL.
Add 20 μg of α-CD134 to the injection solution.
Include 10 μg of α-CD137 in the injection solution.
Inject 100 μL of the prepared solution intraperitoneally (i.p.).
Consider using TLR agonists as alternatives for maintaining antigen-specific CD8+ T cell differentiation and survival.
Wait at least 2 hours after adoptive transfer before performing immunization if done on the same day.
Perform the immunization step within 24 hours after the adoptive transfer to ensure survival of unstimulated CD8+ OT-I cells in vivo.
Start the isolation step on day 4 post-immunization.
Isolate total CD8+ T cells using a bead-based negative selection kit (Dynabeads untouched mouse CD8 cells kit).
Add a cocktail of rat antibodies against non-CD8+ cells to the sample.
Mix magnetic beads coated with anti-rat antibodies into the sample.
Incubate briefly and then use a magnet to separate bead-bound cells from unbound cells.
Perform a second negative selection step using biotinylated α-CD45.2 mAb for highly enriched CD45.1+ CD8+ OT-I cells.
Isolate CD8+ OT-I cells by sorting via flow cytometry.
Resuspend splenocytes in 500 μL of isolation buffer in a 50 mL tube.
Count cells and save an aliquot for flow cytometry analysis.
Add 100 μL of heat-inactivated FBS to the remaining cell suspension.
Mix 100 μL of antibody mix with the cell suspension.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes with rotation.
Wash the cells by adding 10 mL of isolation buffer and mixing well.
Centrifuge the washed cells at 350 g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend depletion beads in isolation buffer by vortexing for >30 seconds.
Transfer 1 mL of resuspended beads to a 15 mL tube.
Add 1 mL of isolation buffer to the bead suspension and mix.
Place the tube with beads on a magnet for 1 minute.
Discard the supernatant after removing the beads from the magnet.
Resuspend washed beads in the same volume as used initially.
Resuspend cells in 4 mL of isolation buffer.
Mix 1 mL of pre-washed beads with the cell suspension.
Incubate this mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes with rotation.
Add 5 mL of isolation buffer to the bead-cell mixture.
Gently pipette the mixture 5 times to resuspend.
Avoid foaming during the resuspension process.
Place the 50 mL tube in the magnet for 2 min.
Pour the supernatant containing the untouched CD8+ T cells into a new sterile 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of isolation buffer and count.
Save an aliquot for flow cytometry analysis to test for purity.
Transfer the cell suspension in a 15 mL tube and add 10 μg of biotinylated α-CD45.2 mAb.
Incubate for 20 min at 4°C with rotation.
Wash cells by adding 2 mL of isolation buffer.
Centrifuge at 350 g for 8 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in isolation buffer to 1 × 10^7/mL.
Vortex biotin binder beads (coated with recombinant streptavidin) for >30 s.
Transfer 100 μL of beads to a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 1 mL of isolation buffer and mix.
Place the tube in the magnet for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the washed beads in the same volume used in step b.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C with rotation.
Add 1 mL of isolation buffer to limit trapping of unbound cells.
Place the 15 mL tube in the magnet for 2 min.
Pour the supernatant containing the untouched CD45.1+ CD8+ T cells into a new tube.
Count the cells.
Set up the Seahorse Analyzer by opening the glycolysis stress test template in Wave software and adding experimental details.
Supplement Seahorse XF DMEM medium pH 7.4 with no phenol red with 2 mM glutamine.
Remove sensor cartridge from 37°C non-CO2 incubator, aspirate dH2O from utility plate, and add 200 μL/well of warm calibrant.
Leave the setup in the incubator for 45-60 minutes.
Centrifuge isolated CD8+ OT-I cells at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in Seahorse medium at a concentration of 6 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Dispense 50 μL of cell suspension to each well, ensuring three technical replicates per sample.
Dispense 50 μL of medium with no cells in the background wells.
Centrifuge plate at 200 g for 1 minute without brake.
Place the plate in a 37°C non-CO2 incubator for 15–25 minutes.
Take the sensor cartridge out from the incubator and add the compounds.
Remove the plate from the incubator and check with a microscope that the cells are attached to the bottom of the wells.
Slowly add 125 μL of Seahorse medium without disturbing the cells.
Return the plate to the 37°C non-CO2 incubator for 15–25 minutes.
Insert the sensor cartridge with the utility plate in the Seahorse analyzer and start calibration.
Once calibration is over, discard the utility plate and insert the cell plate into the machine.
Start the assay.
Analyze data.
Use GraphPad Prism for analysis.
Normalize data if wells do not contain the same number of cells or if treatments affect cell proliferation.
Perform normalization using protein quantification or DNA content Hoechst staining.
Titrate oligomycin to select the minimum concentration needed to achieve a maximal increase in ECAR.
